protocol.adoption: Adopt only on evidence of changed text-transport/check behavior and preserved delivery; shared success/no difference or regression is valid. Do not infer fewer actual user prompts or adoption from author checks.

proposedButNotAdopted.codingMethod: When Windows tools handle non-ASCII text, distinguish script decoding, native-pipe encoding and output-file encoding. Prefer file-based edits with explicit encodings; an unverified native pipe can replace characters before UTF-8 Python or file output sees them. Preserve a BOM where the existing reader needs it, such as a non-ASCII .ps1 in Windows PowerShell. Read back the actual saved artifact and compare important literals with the original or an independently encoded expectation, not an expected value sent through the same pipe. Restore lost text from its source; preserve legitimate question marks. Do not change global profiles to fix a local artifact. See [Microsoft's encoding reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_character_encoding?view=powershell-5.1).
proposedButNotAdopted.conditionalLink: For Windows script/file edits containing non-ASCII text, apply the text-transport method in the [coding lens](domain-lenses.md#coding) before writing or checking the artifact.
